text: I'll start with the paged workload.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The inventory-sync worker runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync in namespace inventory, but the only RoleBinding in that namespace, inventory-reader-binding, lists its subject as ServiceAccount "inventory-synk" — a name that does not exist in the namespace (only "default" and "inventory-sync" do). Because the running identity is never bound to Role/inventory-reader (which grants get/list on configmaps), the worker's API reads are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden, so it cannot refresh the feed and keeps serving the stale inventory snapshot, which is what the data-freshness monitor paged on.
arguments.mechanism: RoleBinding inventory-reader-binding in namespace inventory has .subjects[0].name set to "inventory-synk" instead of "inventory-sync", the ServiceAccount the Deployment actually runs as (.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName). With no binding for that identity, the Role inventory-reader (get/list on configmaps) is never granted to it and the worker's fetch is rejected by the API server with "HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden", after which it falls back to serving the stale snapshot.

evidence.claim: Inventory counts are stale because the worker's fetch is refused and it falls back to the old snapshot.
evidence.quote: sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

evidence.claim: The worker explicitly reports serving stale data, matching the page.
The Deployment runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync.
The only RoleBinding names a subject that does not match the running ServiceAccount.
No ServiceAccount named inventory-synk exists in the namespace, so the binding grants nothing.
evidence.quote: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

evidence.claim: The RoleBinding subject is literally the typo'd name in the object spec.
The Role that would have authorized the worker's configmap reads exists and grants get/list on configmaps.

ruled_out.alternative: The worker pod is crashing or unscheduled
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod is Running and Ready with no restarts, so the failure is not pod lifecycle.
ruled_out.quote: pod/inventory-sync-5cf949f7f9-czxsq phase=Running labels={app=inventory-sync, pod-template-hash=5cf949f7f9} node=incident-lab-control-plane sync(ready=True,restarts=0)

ruled_out.alternative: A missing or mis-keyed source ConfigMap (inventory-sources) is starving the worker of its feed URL
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ConfigMap exists with both expected keys, so the data it needs is present; the failure is the authorization refusal.

ruled_out.alternative: The Role itself lacks the verbs the worker needs
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Role inventory-reader already grants get and list on configmaps, so the permission set is adequate once it reaches the right subject.

verification.command: kubectl -n inventory get rolebinding inventory-reader-binding -o jsonpath='{.subjects[0].name}'

verification.must_contain: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

arguments.root_cause_statement: The inventory-sync worker runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync in namespace inventory, but the only RoleBinding in that namespace, inventory-reader-binding, lists its subject as ServiceAccount "inventory-synk" — a name that does not exist in the namespace (only "default" and "inventory-sync" do). Because the identity the pod actually uses is never bound to any role, its API reads are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden, so the worker cannot refresh the feed and keeps serving the stale inventory snapshot, which is what the data-freshness monitor paged on. Fixing the subject name to inventory-sync restores the grant.
arguments.mechanism: RoleBinding inventory-reader-binding in namespace inventory has .subjects[0].name set to "inventory-synk" instead of "inventory-sync", the ServiceAccount the Deployment actually runs as via .spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName. That identity therefore holds no namespace grant, and the API server rejects the worker's sync fetch with "HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden", after which the worker falls back to serving the previously cached snapshot.

evidence.claim: The worker's fetch is refused with an authorization error.
evidence.quote: sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

evidence.claim: The worker explicitly reports serving stale data, matching the page.
The Deployment runs as ServiceAccount inventory-sync.
The only RoleBinding names a subject that does not match the running ServiceAccount.
No ServiceAccount named inventory-synk exists in the namespace, so the binding grants nothing to anyone.
evidence.quote: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

evidence.claim: The RoleBinding spec literally carries the mistyped subject name.

ruled_out.alternative: The worker pod is crashing, restarting or unscheduled

ruled_out.alternative: A missing or mis-keyed source ConfigMap (inventory-sources) is starving the worker of its feed URL
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ConfigMap exists with both expected keys, so the configuration data it needs is present.

verification.must_contain: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync
